## Best current EMBL group-leader fits

I found **three current EMBL group leaders** whose research is relevant to Priya’s stated interests in computational biology, single-cell analysis, host–pathogen interactions, and reproducible genomics. The strongest overall fit is **Nassos Typas**, followed by **Oliver Stegle** and **Peer Bork**.

| Group leader | Current affiliation | Evidence of scientific fit | Evidence of accepting PhD students |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Nassos Typas** | Head of Molecular Systems Biology, EMBL Heidelberg | His group studies systems microbiology, bacterial cellular networks, microbiomes, and explicitly investigates the **host–pathogen interface**, including Salmonella infection, host responses, pathogen metabolism, and bacterial–phage interactions. This is the closest match to Priya’s host–pathogen goals, although the group’s work is more bacterial systems biology than single-cell host transcriptomics. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/groups/typas/?utm_source=openai)) | **Strong evidence.** Typas is listed on EMBL’s current “Recruiting Group Leaders” page for the EMBL International PhD Programme. The page states that listed groups are actively looking to hire PhD students. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/about/info/embl-international-phd-programme/recruiting-group-leaders/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Oliver Stegle** | EMBL Heidelberg / DKFZ, Heidelberg | The Stegle group develops statistical and machine-learning methods for high-dimensional molecular data, including **single-cell**, spatial, and multi-omics data. This aligns very well with Priya’s scRNA-seq, Bayesian-modelling, R/Python, and reproducible computational-workflow background. The biological focus is broad rather than specifically infectious disease or host–pathogen biology. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/groups/stegle/?utm_source=openai)) | **Strong evidence.** Stegle is listed among the current recruiting EMBL groups, and the group’s Join Us page specifically directs PhD applicants to the EMBL International PhD Programme. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/about/info/embl-international-phd-programme/recruiting-group-leaders/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Peer Bork** | Group Leader and Director of Scientific Activities, EMBL Heidelberg | The Bork group performs computational analysis of microbiome data across genes, proteins, cells, and microbial communities, using large-scale metagenomic and multi-omics datasets. Its work on microbial communities, disease biomarkers, drug–microbe interactions, and microbial ecology could support a host–microbiome or pathogen-genomics direction. The fit to single-cell host–pathogen work is indirect compared with Typas and Stegle. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/groups/bork/?utm_source=openai)) | **No verified current PhD-recruitment evidence found.** The current EMBL recruiting-group list does not list Bork, and the group’s open-positions page describes Bachelor’s/Master’s opportunities but does not establish an active PhD opening. Do not present Bork as currently accepting PhD students without direct confirmation. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/about/info/embl-international-phd-programme/recruiting-group-leaders/?utm_source=openai)) |

### Recommended prioritisation

1. **Nassos Typas — highest thematic fit and current recruitment evidence.**  
   Best choice if Priya wants to connect computational genomics and single-cell expertise to bacterial infection, pathogen physiology, and host–pathogen systems.

2. **Oliver Stegle — strongest methods fit and current recruitment evidence.**  
   Best choice for a quantitatively focused PhD centred on single-cell/spatial analysis, statistical genetics, machine learning, and scalable workflows. A host–pathogen application would likely need to be developed through collaboration or a suitable project rather than assumed from the group’s core biological programme.

3. **Peer Bork — relevant computational microbiome alternative, but recruitment unverified.**  
   Worth considering for microbial community, microbiome, pathogen surveillance, and multi-omics work, but there is currently no official evidence that he is accepting PhD students in the relevant recruitment round.

### Programme and timing note

The EMBL International PhD Programme’s **2026 Summer Recruitment closed on March 9, 2026**. EMBL states that the next round, **2027 Winter Recruitment, opens in September 2026**. EMBL’s recruitment page also explains that applicants indicate research-group preferences, while recruiting Group Leaders review eligible applications and select candidates for interviews. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/about/info/embl-international-phd-programme/application/?utm_source=openai))

**Bottom line:** Priya should prioritise **Typas and Stegle** in the next EMBL application round. Bork is a scientifically plausible third option, but his student-acceptance status should be treated as **unknown**, not inferred from his affiliation or research profile.

His Join Us page explicitly directs PhD applicants to the EMBL International PhD Programme and says the group is always looking for new talent. Stegle is listed among current recruiting group leaders. citeturn0search0turn0search4turn0search6

His group combines quantitative single-cell microscopy, functional genomics, CRISPR libraries, experimental evolution, and modelling to study predator–prey microbial interactions, with explicit interest in the emergence of host–pathogen and host–symbiont interactions. His official Open Positions page welcomes PhD applicants, although the current EMBL central recruiting list does not list him; therefore, direct group-level openness is evidenced, but participation in the current central PhD recruitment round is not verified. citeturn1search1turn1search5turn0search6

sections.body: As of August 8, 2026, EMBL states that 2026 PhD Summer Recruitment is closed and that the next application round opens in September 2026. citeturn0search10
